# bowl_1

## Part plan and resulting asset
One rigid part, `bowl_1__body`: a gently oval wooden serving bowl with a rounded exterior, broad softened rim, closed thick wall, hollow interior and small flat underside. No joints. Bread, plastic wrapping, hands and background objects are excluded. The hand-held photographs establish the wall/rim character and olive-wood appearance; their poses are unknown.

The visual mesh has 48,640 triangles and is watertight. All coordinates are metres. The OBJ part and collision meshes use +Z up, with the origin at the centre of the underside. Blender exports the GLB using the standard glTF Y-up conversion. The GLB contains one mesh and three embedded textures; the Blender file also contains calibrated cameras, lights and hidden collision proxies.

## Scale and shape review
The input reconstruction reports 0.242 × 0.252 × 0.096 m. This was the initial shape. With the supplied camera matrices held fixed, its approximate outer-silhouette IoUs were 0.803, 0.653 and 0.813. A fuller lower wall and increased diameter improved the camera alignment. The retained mesh is approximately **0.2781 × 0.2821 × 0.0891 m**. This is an image-fit adjustment, not an additional physical measurement; calibration/pose uncertainty can also explain some of the discrepancy. `shape.json` records the parameters, which are also the defaults in `build.py`.

Final render-alpha versus convex-hull-of-segmentation IoUs are approximately:

| View | Full outer silhouette | Lower half only |
|---|---:|---:|
| view_0 | 0.969 | 0.961 |
| view_1 | 0.807 | 0.915 |
| view_2 | 0.906 | 0.883 |

The lower-half metric uses the explicit image region y >= 0.5 × image height. It is reported separately, not substituted for the full-frame result. Mask 0 largely includes the bowl's occupied footprint, whereas masks 1 and 2 exclude much of the bread. Consequently raw mask IoU is not a fair measure of the empty bowl's full silhouette. Both raw and adjusted metrics are retained in `review_metrics.json`. The close cropped view does not attain 0.85 over the full outer silhouette. The bottom/side outlines agree better than the occluded top.

`review.jpg` includes source and render for every calibrated view. For the four null-pose entries it explicitly pairs the source with a generic asset overview, not a claimed calibrated render. Renders have a transparent background composited over gray. No supplied camera extrinsics or intrinsics were optimized.

## Surface appearance
Three 2048² PNG PBR maps provide base color, roughness and a subtle grain normal. Metallic is zero. The most reliable calibrated front photograph anchors the visible knot/vein pattern. Unseen surfaces reuse spatially remapped photographic wood, blended with analytic grain. These regions are plausible inferred texture, not recovered backside or interior appearance. The maps retain some original lighting and motion blur; broad grain placement on hidden areas and the precise appearance of the close view remain approximate. Interior depth and the underside are inferred because bread conceals them. The rounded rim is approximately 12–14 mm thick and the central floor about 13 mm thick.

## Contact and physical assumptions
`collision/0.obj` is a convex base; `collision/1.obj` through `7.obj` are convex wall sectors. All are closed solids. They are child rigid bodies under the body's Blender COMPOUND collision shape. The collider preserves an open cavity, but seven angular sectors introduce planar contact facets and the convex wall chords fill part of the lower curved cavity. The base collider top is approximately 20.5 mm above the underside, versus about 13 mm for the visual floor. These proxies suit coarse placement and contact; they do not reproduce detailed contact with small objects or compliant wood.

Density is an assumed 850 kg/m³. Visual solid volume is approximately 0.0009312 m³, giving an assumed mass of 0.792 kg; do not infer mass from the conservatively filled collision volume. Friction is 0.5, restitution 0, and Bullet margin 1 mm. Density, mass, friction, stiffness and restitution were not physically measured. No articulation, deformation or fracture is modeled.

An offline Bullet smoke check drops the bowl onto a plane and a 24 mm sphere into the cavity over 300 frames at 60 fps, with four substeps/frame. The bowl and sphere settle without falling through. `physics_validation.json` records the actual final positions and wall time; this is a basic simulation check, not validated real-world dynamics or an online-estimation benchmark.

## Reproduction and timing
Run `~/blender/blender -b -P build.py`. The builder recreates meshes, collision solids, baked maps, OBJ/GLB/Blend exports and calibrated renders. It invokes `review.py` using an available local Python with Pillow, numpy and scipy; that helper may also be run separately. Run Blender with `-b -P validate_physics.py` to repeat the independent physics smoke check without altering the saved asset.

`validation.json` records mesh checks and actual build/render wall time for the final run. Review layout and the independent smoke check are separate from that interval. This work is an offline asset reconstruction from existing photographs. No new capture, synchronized reconstruction video, online estimation, camera trajectory recovery or website publication is claimed. The files are delivered in the object folder requested for this task.
limitations: Single rigid hollow wooden serving bowl; bread and packaging excluded.

One convex base and seven convex wall sectors form the compound collider; wall chords conservatively fill part of the lower cavity.
Friction 0.5, restitution 0 assumed; no properties experimentally measured.
Photo-projected exterior grain retains source lighting; hidden surfaces use spatially remapped photographed wood mixed with procedural grain, not recovered hidden texture.
